Solutions for Level D: Item Usage.

Concept Overview

  • Polymorphism: Different items have different effects, but use the same `use_item` method signature.
  • Conditional Logic: `if item_id == "med_patch":` checks.

Common Misconceptions

1. String Comparison

Ensure they match the item ID exactly ("med_patch", not "MedPatch").

2. Target Validation

The spec says `if target == "self"`. Students often forget this check, allowing them to heal enemies!

Solution Code

    # Inside Player class
    
    def use_item(self, item_id, target):
        # 1. Check possession
        if not self.inventory.has_item(item_id):
            return f"You don't have '{item_id}'."

        # 2. Handle Med Patch
        if item_id == "med_patch" and target == "self":
            self.heal(20)  # Reuses existing method!
            self.inventory.consume(item_id)
            return "You apply the med patch. +20 HP."

        # 3. Default fallback
        return f"You use the {item_id} on the {target}."
